hookups.source: No operator page exists (kitshillsidecampandcabins.com does not resolve in DNS, 2026-10-22; also ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED on 2026-10-16). The stored water/sewer were derived from note prose resting on a Hipcamp listing and reviews (no such Hipcamp listing could be found today), so they are cleared.

sites.source: Same as hookups: the 'all pull-thru' claim rests only on directory/listing prose; no operator page exists (checked 2026-10-22).

note: Private family-run campground at 6170 100th Ave outside Evart (distinct from Evart's city Riverside Park), on spacious grassy ground; also primitive/tent sites, 5 small cabins and a ~2-acre swim/trout pond. Book by phone. Its old website no longer resolves (2026-10-22); Google lists it as Hillside Campground. Directory listings (not the operator) describe full-hookup pull-through RV sites. --Claude
summary: Operator website kitshillsidecampandcabins.com no longer resolves (DNS gone; same on 2026-10-16) and no Hipcamp listing could be found. Google Maps: 'Hillside Campground', 6170 100th Ave, 4.9 stars / 55 reviews, phone 231-734-2643 (matches), so presence passes on Google and price on RV Life's $$ tier. Cleared the derived water/sewer/pull-through (directory-only). The property is advertised for sale on Crexi/BizQuest as a 20-acre seasonal park. No gateway within 40 km (Grand Rapids 109 km); the family has not stayed here.
flags: Dead website: http://www.kitshillsidecampandcabins.com/ does not resolve (2026-10-22). Google Maps lists the place as 'Hillside Campground' with phone 231-734-2643 but its website link is an unrelated spam domain (eliteus.cyou), so there is no operator website to substitute. Presence rests on Google alone: 4.9 stars / 55 reviews, phone matches (gm.py does not show open/closed status; worth a glance).
Name: Google and RV Life call it 'Hillside Campground' (Crexi/BizQuest: 'Hillside Campground Resort'), not 'Kit's Hillside Camp & Cabins'.

Possibly seasonal/for sale: Crexi and BizQuest (directory/sale listings, undated) advertise 'Hillside Campground Resort' for $1.4M as a 20-acre seasonal park with 45 sites and 5 rental cabins, operating about four months a year. No operator statement of the nightly vs seasonal split or any posted nightly rate exists; RV Life reviews (2019, 2024) report about $35-40 a night. If the park is seasonal in character it fails long-stay test 2 (no posted nightly rate, no booking engine).
